business_scope.primary_industry_name: GPS-Sealed Bonded Road Feeder Service for International Airports

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Code of Obligations; cantonal and federal Commercial Register system; no common-law doctrine of equity)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments Agreement (signed 27 January 2009; entered into force 2010)
Switzerland-China Double Taxation Agreement (current version including the 2013 amending protocol; reduced withholding tax rates applicable)
Switzerland-European Union Free Trade Agreement (1972); EFTA Convention instruments
Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Hague Apostille Convention; effective for Switzerland since 11 February 1973)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: SR 220 (Swiss Code of Obligations), arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft) and arts. 697-697k (share register; non-public UBO disclosure to the company); SR 955.0 (Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, AMLA/GwG), arts. 3-9; SR 955.01 (AMLO); SR 221.411 (Ordinance on the Commercial Register, HRegV); SR 311.0 (Swiss Criminal Code), arts. 305bis and 305ter; SR 946.231 (Embargo Act, international sanctions). A new Federal Act on the Identification of Beneficial Owners of Companies (non-public transparency register with access for authorities and financial intermediaries) is in phased implementation.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (company-internal share register; not public); financial intermediaries must obtain UBO declarations under AMLA; the forthcoming state transparency register remains non-public.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank or PostFinance with blocked capital account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct bank confirmation to the Swiss notary (no apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder's certificate of incorporation and current register extract (for corporate founder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Register authority of the founding company's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing of the corporate founder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registrar or registration agency of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Convention states, Swiss consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or consular officer of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarized copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized power of attorney for the Swiss notary/fiduciary, with specimen signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary of the jurisdiction of origin (for corporate founders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn translation into German

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and signatories against the UN consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions list and EU consolidated list; PEP and close-associate enhanced due diligence under AMLA art. 6; adverse-media and source-of-funds verification; ongoing re-screening at least every six months; heightened origin tracing for virtual-asset-related funding in the Zug 'Crypto Valley' context.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX - Swiss Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch; operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office, EHRA) and the Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug (Handelsregisteramt) for formal name clearance at incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The firm name must conform to arts. 944-956 CO and may use only official Swiss languages (Canton Zug: German) or a mandatory Latin-script transliteration of foreign terms; the legal-form suffix must correspond to the statutory language of the articles (in this case 'AG'); the name must be distinctive, non-misleading and must not infringe the rights of third parties; any foreign-language descriptive element requires a recorded German/Latin transliteration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Schweiz / Eidgenossenschaft / Federal / Bund (prohibited state-affiliation implication)
Trust / Trustee (licensing under the Swiss trustees regime; enhanced regulatory scrutiny)
Fund / Fonds / Investment (CISA collective-scheme approval required)
Audit / Revisionsstelle (audit licensing and supervisory scheme required)
Zoll / Customs / Douane (must not suggest affiliation with the Swiss Federal Customs Administration; permissible only as a descriptive activity element)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No nationwide statutory name reservation exists in Switzerland; a rejected name may be revised and re-submitted immediately without additional fees. If the Commercial Register issues a formal negative ruling, the applicant may file written opposition with the register office within the statutory deadline and thereafter appeal to the cantonal register supervisory authority and the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) under VwVG, with final appeal to the Federal Supreme Court. Pre-verification of available names on ZEFIX and an early informal consultation letter from the Canton Zug register office materially reduce rejection risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Mail-drop addresses are formally tolerated if the registered office can receive legal documents; however, for customs-bonded road transport under ISIC 5222, the Federal Customs Act (SR 631.0) and associated customs ordinances require a physical operational base in Switzerland (vehicle yard, cargo documentation and control premises, driver facilities). A fiduciary letter-box alone would fail commercial substance expectations and customs-license audit tests; recommended structure: lease at least one operating premises in the Zug/Lucerne economic area and register the GPS-customs-sealed fleet there.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: CUSTOMS: HIGH - the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (FOCBS/BAZG) conducts announced and unannounced on-site inspections of bonded transit operators, generally at least once within 24 months of authorization, with GPS-sealed cargo movement data and registry audits; REGISTERED OFFICE: LOW - unannounced physical inspection of the registered office by the Commercial Register occurs with less than 5% probability per year in the absence of irregular filings or adverse AML indicators.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name pre-verification and preliminary clearance check via ZEFIX and Canton Zug Commercial Register (Firmenname-Vorbescheid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per art. 4 HRegV and cantonal fee catalogue (approx. CHF 150-200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the deed of incorporation and articles of association, including capital deposit confirmation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss civil-law notary in Canton Zug
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff and market benchmark (approx. CHF 1,000-2,500 depending on share capital and drafting complexity)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register entry fees (cantonal and federal EHRA) plus SHAB official gazette publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Register of Canton Zug / Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per art. 5 HRegV and federal fee ordinance (approx. CHF 600-900 inclusive)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and, where required, consular legalization of the founder/UBO dossier (certificate of incorporation, good standing, passport copies, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the country of origin; Swiss consular section for non-Hague states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or fixed per-document fee (approx. USD 80-150 per document; 2-3 documents expected)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translations into German (statutes, apostilled founder documents, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translation bureau or certified translator in Canton Zug
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of the Swiss Association of Certified Translators (approx. CHF 120-250 per standard document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance and UBO penetration package: KYC forms, PEP/OFAC/UN/SECO screening, source-of-funds verification, AML risk classification memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed fiduciary or financial intermediary acting as AML gatekeeper for the corporate account opening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard corporate structure with two UBOs (approx. CHF 450-750)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and correspondence services in Canton Zug (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for registered-office service with mail handling and corporate-housekeeping (approx. CHF 1,500-2,500 per year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customs client registration with FOCBS/BAZG and facilitation of the customs guarantee arrangement for the bonded truck fleet (cover, bonding, license dossier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Customs Administration (FOCBS/BAZG) and issuing bank for the customs guarantee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee is nominal (nil to CHF 100); guarantee issuance is based on bank commission (approx. CHF 700-1,200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory pre-notifications for airport feeder/road transport operations, aviation-security handling, data-protection (FADP) record, and continuity file for licensing under the Customs Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Office for Customs / cantonal transport licensing authority (Kanton Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative tariff per cantonal and federal fee ordinances (approx. CHF 250-450)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) of 30 March 1911, Articles 620-763, in particular Articles 626-632 (founders and incorporation), Article 629 (minimum capital), Article 630 (paid-up capital), Articles 634-640 (articles of incorporation and reports), Article 716 (board of directors) and Article 718 (power to bind the company); supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411) and the revised Swiss company law effective 1 January 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) competent for the seat canton, operating under the central eGRIS/Zefix platform and the federal supervision of the Federal Commercial Register Law Office (EHRA) of the Federal Office of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Errichtungsakt) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten), plus the electronic registration application to the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) and certified specimen signature cards.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An Aktiengesellschaft requires minimum share capital of CHF 100,000, with no nominal share lower than CHF 0.01. At incorporation at least 20% of the nominal capital, but not less than CHF 50,000, must be paid-up in cash and irrevocably placed at the disposal of the company in a notary-controlled blocked account (Sperrkonto); release occurs only upon successful commercial register entry. Contributions in kind (e.g., the bonded truck fleet) require a statutory audit report confirming the asset valuation; no bearer shares are permissible and founders must declare all non-cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously by the Board of Directors of CH_AG convened on [date] at [registered office address], Switzerland: 1. Acceptance of the founders' share subscription in the total amount of CHF 100,000; subscription instruments are filed with the minutes. 2. Establishment of the registered office of the Company at [address]; the address is hereby approved. 3. Adoption of the Articles of Association as drafted and notarized. 4. Electing [Name] as Chairman and [Name], [Name] as other directors, each with sole signatory authority; all appointments take effect upon commercial register entry. 5. Confirmation of the paid capital of CHF 50,000 blocked in a Swiss escrow account. The Board instructs the Chairman to execute all notarial filings and the commercial register application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance and legal-form validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix official Swiss Commercial Register search portal; Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the intended seat canton.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a Zefix search on the proposed name 'CH_AG' to verify availability and absence of conflicting trade names; confirm that the legal-form suffix 'AG' is used correctly and that no protected brand is infringed; file a name-reservation request or obtain a preliminary name-availability confirmation from the cantonal commercial registry; secure the exact legal-entity name for the notarial deeds.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name with legal-form suffix 'AG'
Zefix search result printout
Evidence of intended seat canton and registered office municipality
Founder identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a conflict or confusion notice, file a written objection or amend the name with a distinctive geographic or business-scope reference; if the conflict is patent, re-submit a new name application; unresolved disputes may be referred to the Federal Commercial Register Law Office (EHRA).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the blocked capital escrow account and minimum capital payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank holding the blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the future AG or under the notary's incorporation mandate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) referencing the future AG; pay in the minimum CHF 50,000 by final, irrevocable transfer from the subscribers; obtain the bank's written confirmation that the funds are unencumbered and blocked for the purpose of incorporation; agree that the balance may be released only upon completion of the commercial register entry or upon refusal of the registration by the competent authority.
required_dossiers: Bank account application of the future AG or notarial block-account mandate
Notarial mandate letter specifying the Sperrkonto purpose
Proof of origin of funds and AML declaration
Founder and ultimate beneficial owner identification set
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML or beneficial-ownership questions, supply a detailed declaration of origin and chain of fund transfers; alternatively, provide a bank guarantee issued by a FINMA-licensed bank as a valid substitute for the cash payment; any correction of the attestation is obtained directly from the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation and adoption of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal public notary (Notar / notaire) competent for the registered office of the company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the draft Articles of Association and the incorporation deed to the notary; the notary authenticates the identity and signatures of all founders, establishes the resolutions (share subscription, adoption of articles, registered office, initial officers) in a notarial minute, verifies the paid-up amount against the bank attestation and checks the statutory suitability of the directors; after reading of the final text, all subscribers sign the notarized deed.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) in an official Swiss language or with authorized translation
Bank confirmation of the blocked escrow capital
Passport or identity card of each founder and appointed director
Consent letter of the registered office property owner (Zustimmung des Sitzvermieters)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal deficiencies, correct the Articles of Association by an addendum or prepare a revised draft and re-notarize in the same session; any post-execution amendments must be documented in a separate notarial minute before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register application, statutory examination and registry fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) acting through the eGRIS workflow of the federal Commercial Register platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the eGRIS registration application within the statutory period after notarization; upload the notarial deed, Articles of Association, specimen signature cards, seat-owner consent, tax-seat declaration and the finalized list of directors with managing authority; pay the cantonal registry fee (approximately CHF 700-1,200) plus SHAB publication cost; the registrar examines the lawfulness of the business object, capital payment, officers and seat documentation and, upon approval, orders the entry and publication.
required_dossiers: eGRIS application signed by the Chairman and one further director with notarized signature validity
Notarized deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
Certified specimen signature cards
Consent declaration of the registered office owner
Tax-seat statement and registered office confirmation
Registry fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues deficiency interrogatories, cure the points within 10 to 15 days by supplementary statements; if rejection is threatened, submit a written objection to the cantonal Commercial Register authority and alternatively appeal to the Federal Commercial Register Law Office (EHRA) within 30 days of the refusal decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal personality, UID allocation and SHAB publication confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register; Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/FOSC); Federal Statistical Office and Federal Tax Administration for the company identification number (UID).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon the statutory entry, the cantonal registry issues the certified Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) stating the legal form, share capital and officers; the UID number is automatically assigned and the entry is published in SHAB/FOSC; the Aktiengesellschaft acquires legal personality as of the commercial register entry (Article 643 CO); retrieve the electronic extract and publication notice and forward them to banks, insurers and business partners.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
UID-number confirmation issued through the eGRIS/ESTV gateway
SHAB/FOSC publication notice
Bank release instruction for the blocked capital account after entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extract contains errors, request an ex officio rectification from the cantonal registry; if the UID is missing, require immediate allocation; any interested party may challenge the entry within the legal observation period and seek restoration of rights before the EHRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social insurance and customs-authorization qualification post-registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV) for VAT; cantonal tax administration for corporate income and capital tax; cantonal old-age and survivors' insurance compensation office (AHV/AVS) together with SUVA for employer accident insurance; Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG) for bonded-customs qualifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the UID has been transmitted to all tax authorities and that corporate income tax and VAT registrations are effective; register as an employer with the cantonal compensation office for social insurance contributions and with SUVA for compulsory accident insurance of all employees; in parallel, submit the application for the customs bonded warehouse operator authorization and the professional road freight transport licence to the FOCBS, since a Swiss-registered legal entity with a valid UID is a prerequisite for the customs licence; confirm the parking and depot clearances for the truck fleet.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract and Articles of Association
Officer identification data and police certificate of good conduct where required
Employer registration form for the compensation office and SUVA
UID and tax status confirmation
FOCBS customs licence application with fleet, security and GPS-seal documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration lags, file a written initial registration with the FTA; if the UID is not recognized by the tax gateway, request activation through the ESTV portal; employer-registration disputes are resolved by the cantonal compensation office; customs-licence rejections may be appealed through the FOCBS formal remedy procedure within the statutory appeal period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS / BAZG) as lead federal authority for the customs-bonded trucking licence; Cantonal Freight Transport Licensing Unit for the professional road transport licence; Cantonal Building and Fire Inspectorate for depot clearances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Bonded Warehouse Operation and Sealed International Road-Feeder Transport Licence (Zolllager- und Zollgutbeförderungsbewilligung) under Articles 24 ff. of the Customs Ordinance (SR 631.0) together with the professional road freight transport licence under the Swiss Goods Transport Ordinance (AVEV, SR 742.111).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU), assisted by the competent Cantonal Environmental Protection Office for the registered office and depot site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - simplified environmental registration / EIA pre-screening; no full EIA report is required for a bonded truck fleet or freight depot unless the annex thresholds of the Swiss EIA Ordinance (EUV/UIAA) are exceeded, such as very large parking or terminal hard-surface areas subject to a cantonal building permit; the applicant obtains the environmental registry stamp within the building-permit procedure.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance enforced under the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1): PM10 exhaust emissions in stationary abatement installations limited to 10 mg/m³; VOC exhaust air in fuel-handling and cleaning stations limited to 20 mg C/m³ when abated, with a 150 mg C/m³ ceiling where recovery is waived; hydrocarbon-laden wastewater requires oil-separator proof and a cantonal discharge permit (Einleitbewilligung); waste oils, filters and soot must be consigned as special waste under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600) with manifests and disposal certificates; night-time noise at the depot boundary respects the Noise Abatement Ordinance limit values, typically 50 dB(A) in residential receiving zones and 60 dB(A) in industrial zones.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification and structural-load inspection for the fleet depot premises issued by the cantonal fire brigade and building inspectorate as a condition of the building permit; occupational-safety clearance under Article 82 of the Swiss Federal Accident Insurance Act (UVG) with SUVA and EKAS; workplace risk assessment covering forklift and maintenance-bay safety, ergonomic lifting and driver-fatigue management; mandatory tachograph and driver-hours audits by the Federal Roads Office (ASTRA) and cantonal police; civil-defence parking-space liability confirmed where the depot exceeds the statutory threshold.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV), Bern — official portal: www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) must first complete commercial registry registration at the cantonal commercial register office. The cantonal tax authority (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) automatically assigns the corporate UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / IDI) which serves as the VAT ID and tax reference number. For non-resident entities without a Swiss establishment, VAT registration is required under Art. 14 Swiss VAT Law (MWSTG) by submitting Form 32 to the FTA, with a written or online application via the Swiss VAT portal (E-Service VAT). A non-resident company may appoint a Swiss fiscal representative or use the electronic VAT settlement procedure if turnover exceeds the registration threshold or supplies taxable services in Switzerland. No statutory tax identification card is issued; the UID is published in the Swiss UID register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Swiss AG is subject to federal corporate income tax (effective flat 8.5% on net profit after tax surcharges), cantonal and communal profit taxes (combined effective rates typically 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton; subject to tax reform rules), and Swiss net wealth tax for the capital stock. The AG is a tax-resident entity if registered office and effective management are in Switzerland. Territorial scope: Swiss taxes worldwide income for resident AGs, but dividends from qualifying participations are exempt under the 10/30 participation relief rule. No pass-through classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a check-the-box election for tax classification. The AG is inherently a corporately taxed legal entity. Certain statutory elections are available: (1) election to form a group for VAT purposes (VAT group registration under Art. 21 MWSTG) enabling consolidated VAT treatment of affiliated entities; (2) election for reduced VAT taxation on specific supplies; (3) election to apply the Swiss domestic margin scheme for used goods and works of art; (4) in cantonal profit tax, an election may be made for the qualifying participation exemption or notional interest deduction on equity capital (NID) under limited conditions; (5) for federal profit tax, a forward-loss carry-forward election is mandatory. Hybrid mismatch elections under Swiss law are limited to explicit anmeldung (notification) of a selected classification for Swiss tax purposes if incompatible with a foreign classification; no generic check-the-box is permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover from supplies (excluding exempt supplies, but including supplies deemed to be in Switzerland; separate threshold of CHF 100,000 for certain franchises). Non-resident suppliers without establishment in Switzerland are not subject to the threshold and are required to register if performing taxable supplies in Switzerland except where the supply is subject to reverse-charge/deemed-taxed rules. A separate mandatory registration threshold of CHF 10,000 for goods deliveries on consignment in the customs warehouse sector applies if the business is not domiciled in Switzerland.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. E-invoicing is permitted and encouraged under general VAT compliance rules. An e-invoice must contain all mandatory data under Art. 26 MWSTG and be integrity-ensured (e.g., EDI-HAN, XML with qualified electronic signature, or Swiss QR-Rechnung). The Swiss Peer-to-Peer Electronic Invoicing Framework (eBill) is widely used but not legally mandatory. From 1 January 2026, e-billing (Peppol BIS 3.0) will be mandatory for all federal government suppliers, but no national B2B mandate exists. For export transactions, the Swiss customs declaration system (e-dec) and Swiss export declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration) are filed electronically via the Swiss Customs' Galileo system (more recently

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions; no exchange control approval is required for cross-border payments. Profit and dividend remittances are unrestricted, but Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) of 35% applies to dividend distributions, with potential relief under double taxation treaties or via refund procedures. For an AG, distributable reserves must be certified and statutory capital preservation rules observed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland has no forced surrender or conversion of export receipts; proceeds can be held, sold forward, or used in any currency. Enterprises must comply with SNB statistical reporting if their cross-border assets or liabilities exceed reporting thresholds, and SECO economic sanctions require transaction approval for listed persons or countries.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Swiss-regulated fintech banks and payment institutions (FINMA licensure, e.g., the 'Fintech-license' per Art. 1b Banking Act) are viable for low-risk logistics payments. Offshore digital EMIs without a Swiss banking or fintech license cannot legally accept Swiss deposits or provide local IBANs; they may be used only as ancillary transaction rails through a licensed Swiss correspondent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted in Switzerland using FINMA-accepted video identification (qualified electronic signature and notarized corporate documents). However, for non-resident directors, complex ownership, or any PEP/sanctions flag, Swiss banks routinely require physical appearance of at least one director and beneficial owner at a branch interview; for an AG with only Swiss directors, fully virtual opening is possible.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to multi-tier foreign shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charters, conclusive beneficial ownership register (as per Art. 958e CO), passport copies, notarized declarations, trust or foundation structure charts, and financial statements evidencing source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure from cross-border clients or high-risk corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results (SECO/FINMA), end-user certificates for transport contracts, customs/bonded documentation, list of controlled goods, and insurance/incoterm contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cash intensity or unexplained payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed invoicing with ISIC 5222 scope, GPS-sealed tamper-proof assurance reports, route manifests, ACH/direct bank transfer statistics, and audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient substance in Switzerland for an AG
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregister), board minutes, Swiss registered office lease, corporate tax filings (VAT, direct federal tax), payroll/social security enrollments, and actual business operations in bonded trucking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections are routed as SWIFT MT103 or SEPA wire with Purpose Code 'G300' (equity injection). For share capital, funds must be credited to a blocked capital escrow account (Aktienkapitalkonto) at a Swiss bank; the board later calls funds. For shareholder loans, execute a written loan agreement with repayment terms; no SNB approval is required, but SNB statistical reporting thresholds apply to cross-border financial relationships.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 to suppliers, with commercial documentary credits (LC) for large customs-bonded cargo transactions. Payments must match the invoice, use Incoterms, and be accompanied by transport/C-TPAT/TIR carnets. For operational expenses, ACH/SEPA payments via the Swiss SIC system are standard.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic/illiquid currency pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of annual financial statements at the regular General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders General Assembly (internal corporate record; minutes kept at registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end; for calendar-year company the General Meeting must take place by 30 June (CO Article 699)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director civil liability for delayed preparation; cantonal fine for non-compliance with company law; court may order the company be wound up if the defect is serious

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audit report by external statutory auditor (limited review or ordinary audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: External independent auditor (elected by General Meeting; report submitted to board/shareholders, not to Commercial Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the General Meeting deadline (six months after balance-sheet date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Auditor subject to professional liability; absence of audit report makes financial statements invalid for dividend distributions and can trigger tax audit adjustments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (direct federal tax, cantonal and communal taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority of the registered office (e.g., Steueramt Zug); direct federal tax collected via the canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Canton-specific filing deadline, commonly 30 June after the tax year; available extension to 31 October upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default and procedural assessments, late-payment interest of 3.5-4.5 percent per annum, procedural fines up to CHF 20,000, separate criminal penalties for negligent or wilful tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT accounting period; annual filers with 31 December year-end must file and pay by 1 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder charges, 4 percent default interest per annum, administrative penalty up to 25 percent of the tax due (50 percent for gross negligence), criminal proceedings for wilful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/IV/EO/ALV wage declaration and employee Lohnausweis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Lohnausweis to employees by 31 January; employer wage declaration and annual contribution settlement by the compensation office calendar, generally no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory arrears interest on unpaid social security contributions; administrative fines under AHV legislation; debt-collection enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register filings for changes resolved at the annual meeting (directors, auditor, registered office, capital changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the underlying resolution or event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal entry in the register and procedural fines; delayed filing can be enforced as an administrative order and triggers civil liability to creditors if losses result

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit under CO Article 727 is compulsory if, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds two of the three thresholds: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million, gross turnover above CHF 40 million, or annual average of more than 250 full-time employees. Smaller companies require a limited audit (CO 727a) unless all shareholders unanimously waive the audit for a company with fewer than 10 full-time employees (CO 727b).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (CO 958-963); Swiss GAAP FER as the authoritative national framework; IFRS permitted for non-regulated entities and mandatory for listed companies and financial-sector regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company maintains the share register (Aktienbuch/Actionnaire register) at its registered office. Each registered shareholder must state whether the shares are held for a beneficial owner and, if so, provide the owner's data; this declaration is obtained at acquisition and on each transfer and is revalidated annually as part of the audit. No separate annual UBO return is filed with the Commercial Register for private AGs, but the register and declarations must be produced to the auditor and authorities on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Commercial register (official record of board members and authorised signatories)
Minutes of the General Meeting and Board of Directors
Annual financial statements and audit reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 1,500-3,500 (approx USD 1,700-4,000) per year for Swiss registered office/corporate agent, including correspondence and local administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 4,000-12,000 (approx USD 4,500-13,500) for a limited audit review; CHF 15,000-40,000 (approx USD 17,000-45,000) for an ordinary audit depending on fleet size and balance-sheet complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory corporate income tax 8.5% (effective 7.83% after deductibility of the federal tax itself); combined federal, cantonal and communal effective tax burden in Zug approx. 11.9% for a profitable operating AG.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal and municipal tax holidays: up to 100% exemption for up to 10 years for new economically beneficial undertakings (Art. 71 Cantonal Tax Act Zug); no tax holiday at federal level. Holding company privilege: substantial (≥20%) dividend and capital gains participation deduction; no Swiss net wealth tax for qualifying participations. R&D and patent box regimes available in most cantons but not in Zug; not applicable to ISIC 5222 trucking.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal Zug combined tax return: 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Formulaire pour personnes morales' (Form 22) together with the federal direct federal tax schedule ('Staatssteuerklärung B' and federal Form 480); filed electronically via the Zug eTax portal 'tax.zg.ch' (eZug) or via SWISS ITS certified filing software. UID-number and balance sheet data transmitted in the XML/iXBRL format of the Swiss Tax Conference.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal-year return; quarterly provisional tax installments (based on the prior year assessment; corrected upon filing).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the end of the business year, i.e. by 30 June for a 31 December year-end (Zug Cantonal Tax Act Art. 53). An extension of up to 6 months is available upon reasoned request; the federal direct tax return follows the same deadline as the cantonal return (VStG/DBG Art. 124).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss business identification number (UID/CHE) of the AG; cross-reference with the Commercial Register entry and the customs-bonded operator licence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a 100% non-resident-owned AG, supplement with the parent's foreign registration number and, if available, LEI; the Swiss UID remains the sole tax identifier for the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Must be marked 'Aktiengesellschaft (AG)'. Any mis-marking delays the assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Irrelevant to the shareholder; directors, even if foreign-resident, must sign the declaration electronically with Swiss tax-ID of their mandate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered seat in Switzerland with actual business address; a pure post-box in Zug is a fatal substance flag.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the place of effective management is outside Switzerland, the AG is treated as non-resident and the return must include a separate statement of the foreign management location, triggering risk of full re-allocation of trucking income abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets per audited Swiss balance sheet; basis for the capital tax (Zug rate approx. 0.06% per annum).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Debt to the foreign parent must be disclosed; a related-party loan exceeding 3:1 debt-to-equity with interest above arm's length will be recharacterized as hidden equity distribution and hit by a 35% retro-dividend tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, AHV-declared wages and social contributions of the Swiss drivers and dispatchers; must correspond to the social security declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the registered drivers are resident abroad (e.g., non-resident owner-operator subcontractors), the tax authority will require proof of the permanent establishment of the truck fleet and apply payroll withholding tax at source; non-declaration constitutes criminal tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of the bonded truck fleet is limited to 20% diminishing-balance for road vehicles and 10% for terminal I.T. equipment; excessive depreciation will be added back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directives require equal treatment of the Swiss fleet and leased assets from the foreign parent; intercompany leasing rates must be documented in the TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercially booked net profit per individual income statement for the 12-month period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intra-group charges from the foreign parent (fleet management, GPS tracking, insurance) must be supported by the arm's-length benchmarks; otherwise a 20% to 50% upwards adjustment and default interest are applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit after correction of non-deductible items and depreciation adjustments; the basis for federal tax at 8.5% (effective 7.83%) and cantonal/communal income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent must include a statement of the Swiss permanent-establishment profit share if the AG's fleet also services routes across the Swiss border; cross-border cost apportionment to the foreign PE must be set out in the TP report.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: disciplinary fine up to CHF 1,500 (Zug StG Art. 53) and up to CHF 10,000 federal (DBG Art. 237); default interest of 5% per annum on the assessed tax; after reminder, daily surcharge at the authority's discretion. Deliberate non-filing combined with false documents escalates to criminal tax fraud with up to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine up to CHF 500,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss Anticipatory Tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on any dividend distribution by the AG; statutory rate cannot be reduced where the recipient is a Swiss resident company. As of the 2022/2023 reform (OASI reform), a reduced rate of 25% applies to dividends distributed by companies with substantial participations in other Swiss companies when the recipient holds 10% or more for 1 year, but generally the 35% rate applies unless treaty relief is granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For a non-Swiss parent: (i) the distributing Swiss AG must obtain from the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV) a certificate of 'domicile' and file the form 'WS-A' or standard application for repayment of anticipatory tax together with (ii) the parent's tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its home authority and a letter of beneficial ownership; (iii) the application must be filed within the calendar year or, at latest, within 3 years of the dividend payment (Art. 33 (2) VStG); (iv) if the group holds ≥10% of the voting rights of the Swiss AG, the applicable DTA rate is usually 0% (e.g., Switzerland–EU/Swiss–US 0% at ≥10% holding with substance; 15% for portfolio dividends of smaller shareholdings); (v) FTA reimbursement is processed within 30 days at the earliest; the Swiss AG may simultaneously apply for a 'relief at source' permit (Form 823) to pay the reduced treaty rate directly without the full 35% levy. Documentary proof of the beneficial owner's economic substance is mandatory; a shell parent is rejected and the full 35% tax is retained.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory Swiss WHT is 0% on outbound royalties; treaty rates under Swiss DTAs are generally 0% (e.g., OECD-based treaties with most jurisdictions). Debt interest: 35% anticipatory tax applies only to public-bond (Anleihen) interest and certain Swiss-regulated debt instruments; ordinary intercompany and bank interest paid to non-residents is exempt from Swiss withholding tax. However, if the debt is recharacterized as hidden equity (thin capitalization), the interest is treated as a dividend and the 35% tax is levied, with a 10-year retrospective assessment possible.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where the Swiss AG's aggregate cross-border related-party transactions (goods, including fuel, spare parts and fleet services, as well as royalties and interest) exceed CHF 10 million in a fiscal year; also required where related-party domestic transactions exceed CHF 10 million. Master File: required when the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent exceeds CHF 2 billion (OECD BEPS standard). A simplified transactional file (simpler documentation) applies to lower-risk service companies; however, the customs-bonded trucking company is treated as a full-risk operating entity and must file the complete documentation upon request within 30 days.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the BVI/Cayman sense; however, under Federal Direct Tax Act Art. 50 (place of effective management) and FTA administrative practice, an AG claiming treaty benefits and holding the customs-bonded transport licence must prove real economic substance at its registered office: own or rented operational premises in Switzerland, full-time personnel (at least one qualified manager with Swiss residence), the board meeting in and effective management from Switzerland, bookkeeping in Switzerland and valid customs-broker licence (Art. 22 à 25 of the Swiss Customs Ordinance; MOFA/T-Pe operator approval). The absence of substance lets the tax authority either (i) disregard the Swiss entity as a sham and allocate the trucking income to the foreign shareholder's permanent establishment, or (ii) refuse the WHT treaty reduction under the anti-abuse rule. For ISIC 5222, the Swiss customs agency also requires a physical depot, weighbridge access, and a GPS-sealed fleet register; failure to maintain these triggers withdrawal of the customs licence and immediate tax reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate non-declaration or undervaluation of the trucking revenue, cash payments from airport cargo agents not booked, or false accounting of fuel supplies along the customs route.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine of up to the amount of tax evaded (DBG Art. 175); if false invoices or forged documents are used, the qualification is 'criminal tax fraud' (DBG Art. 186) with imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to CHF 500,000; full back-taxes plus default interest of 5% p.a.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CEO and each board member are criminally liable as 'authors of the tax offense' (unlawful instructions do not protect directors); the court may impose a travel ban and asset freeze (Code of Criminal Procedure Art. 237); the tax authority may pierce the corporate veil and order civil restitution against the directors for the unpaid tax where the company is stripped of assets (DBG Art. 12a in respect of withholding tax responsibility).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulation of the GPS-sealed T1/T2 transit declarations, underweighing cargo in the airport feeder operation, unjustified discharge from the customs bond, or smuggling undeclared high-value cargo inside the freight vehicles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs penalty up to 3 times the evaded import duties (Customs Act Art. 118-120); confiscation of the vehicle fleet and the cargo; withdrawal of the bonded warehouse/trucking licence with no re-grant for 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge or negligent supervision are subject to personal fines up to CHF 100,000 and disqualification from customs representation; the customs authority may also arrest the responsible director pending extradition if the cargo crosses borders (travel ban under Art. 237 CCP).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Zug AG with nominal registered office, no employees, no real business activity, the entire management in the hands of the foreign parent, and no physical presence in Switzerland, used solely to hold the Swiss customs licence and to re-invoice flights and trucking profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income re-allocation to the place of effective management abroad; denial of the Swiss DTA relief and of the 0%/15% dividend WHT; capital tax assessment on a fictive equity basis; for the parent, a retroactive withholding tax demand of 35% on the deemed distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The local nominee director (often resident in Zug) is criminally sanctioned for 'employment of a sham domicile' under the Code of Obligations Art. 62i (non-disclosure of the beneficial owner) and the cantonal tax law; fines up to CHF 20,000, personal restitution obligation for taxes lost, and immediate removal from the Commercial Register.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and financial intermediation (client funds in the bonded supply chain)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG acts as an airport feeder and receives consolidated payments from foreign cargo banks, then re-disburses to its parent; a failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the freight transactions (including any crypto/tokenized payments via ACH or wire) and the absence of a FINMA-required license or registered AML CFO.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to CHF 500,000 under the Financial Services Act; for the entity, disqualification from banking relationships; funds are frozen; the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) report leads to a penal inquiry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members of the AG incur personal fines and imprisonment up to 3 years (AML Act Art. 9, SFTA), forfeiture of the frozen assets, and a personal travel ban if they reside abroad; the director's personal assets are attached for the restitution of the laundered value.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaration of Swiss VAT on the road feeder service, false zero-rating of the cross-border transport legs, or misclassifying truck drivers as independent subcontractors to avoid AHV/AVS social contributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Value-added tax amendment of up to 10 years (if fraud) plus a fine of up to 3 times the evaded VAT; social security retro-assessment of unpaid AHV (no statute of limitation) plus contributions and default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Swiss VAT Act Art. 12 and AHV Act Art. 52, directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid VAT/social contributions to the degree of their fault if the company becomes insolvent; the social security authority may secure a civil attachment against the directors' personal bank accounts and impose a prohibition on leaving Switzerland until the debt is settled.
